$comment: The connector taxonomy's one machine-readable source (SMD-1933). docs/connector-taxonomy.md is the spec and carries the tables scripts/connector-registry.ts renders from this file; check-fork-consistency check 19 validates it and holds the two equal. A new external-touching contribution adds an entry here (or an excuse under not_connectors.artifacts, with its reason) — the check finds it by its metadata.json services and tags and by the SMD-1924 disposition table.

direction.note: Per capability. A connector's direction is derived: `bidirectional` when its capabilities span both.

round_trip.note: SMD-1867's canonical-is-truth rule: `writable` means the brain writes the item back to the vendor, so the stored canonical must round-trip.

transport.note: How new data reaches the seam, never a wire protocol. push: the vendor calls in as things happen. pull: the fetcher asks on a schedule or on demand. batch: a one-shot archive or export file. For a sink, how the brain's output reaches the vendor (a send is push).

cardinality.note: Vendor item to thought at the seam. The family names the item and owns the grouping key. An enrichment stage past the seam (atomization, SMD-1930) does not change it.

family.note: The semantic class of the item. Grows as new sources appear; each new family is declared here with its schema before an artifact uses it.

fetchers.low-code-node: a node of the orchestration tool SMD-1863 picks; the default for any vendor the tool exposes
fetchers.native-driver: a typed OB1 script or function that speaks the vendor's protocol itself; the fallback
fetchers.mcp-server: the AI client's own connector — an MCP server or a channel plugin — calling the vendor on demand
fetchers.browser-extension: a client in the user's browser that pushes what the user is looking at

mailbox/email.grouping_key: thread — RFC 2822 Message-ID / In-Reply-To / References, or the vendor's thread id
mailbox/email.canonical: the RFC 2822 message: headers (Message-ID, Date, From, To, Cc, Subject, In-Reply-To, References, List-Id, Labels), the text/plain body, the text/html body, attachment names and types (never bodies)
mailbox/email.text: Subject, From, Date, then the plain body with quoted replies and signatures stripped; the html body flattened only when no plain part exists
edges: correspondent person edges from From/To/Cc (a person entity per address)
reply-to edges along In-Reply-To / References to the thread's other messages
metadata: sensitivity (the fetcher's local routing verdict, when it made one)
mailbox/email.identity: `<vendor>:<account>:<Message-ID>`; the Message-ID survives a label change, a move and a re-download, so a re-pull is a no-op
mailbox/email.dividing_line: a scheduled mailbox pull or a label-triggered push is a stateful workflow → tool node; "draft this digest" or "read this one thread" on demand → the client's MCP connector
mailbox/email.sink_shape: a draft or a send: subject, body, recipients; the brain never edits a message that exists

message-stream/chat.item: one message in a channel or a direct conversation
message-stream/chat.grouping_key: conversation — channel id + thread ts (Slack), channel id + message reference chain (Discord), chat id + reply_to_message_id (Telegram), the DM conversation id (X, Instagram)
message-stream/chat.canonical: the vendor's message object: ids (message, channel or chat, thread or reply-to), author, timestamp, the text with the vendor's markup intact, mentions, reactions, attachment references, an edited timestamp when the vendor keeps one
message-stream/chat.text: the message text with the vendor's markup flattened (mention tokens to display names, formatting to plain text) and the author and channel named once
edges: mention edges to the people and channels named
reply-to edge along the grouping key
message-stream/chat.identity: `<vendor>:<workspace>:<channel>:<message id>` — the vendor's message id is stable across an edit, which is what lets telegram-capture's UPDATE_ON_EDIT re-embed in place
message-stream/chat.dividing_line: a bot that must sit on the vendor's event stream (a webhook receiver, a gateway session) is a stateful workflow → tool node, or a native driver where the tool lacks the vendor; a confirmation reply to the captured message is part of the source capability (an ack), not a sink; a briefing or digest sent on a cadence is the sink capability → tool node when scheduled by the tool, the client's channel plugin when the AI client sends it
message-stream/chat.sink_shape: one outbound message (text, optional media) to a chat id; many thoughts → one message is the digest case (many:1)

conversation-export.item: one conversation with an AI assistant, or one captured exchange of it
conversation-export.grouping_key: conversation id; within it, the turn index and (ChatGPT) the branch the export resolves to
conversation-export.canonical: the vendor's conversation object: conversation id, title, created and updated timestamps, the ordered turns each with role, timestamp, text (markdown intact) and tool or citation blocks, the branch map when the vendor exports one
conversation-export.text: the turns in order as `role: text`, markdown flattened, tool and citation blocks reduced to their visible text
edges: citation edges to the URLs a turn cites
conversation-export.identity: `<vendor>:<conversation id>` for a whole conversation; `<vendor>:<conversation id>:<turn index>` for a captured exchange — the id survives a rename
conversation-export.dividing_line: a one-shot export file is a batch → native driver (a parse has no workflow state for a tool to hold); a browser capture is a push → browser extension; an auto-sync over the vendor's API is a pull the tool owns once SMD-1863 lands. Distilling a conversation into 0–5 thoughts is an enrichment past the seam; the recipes that do it today declare `1:many` because that is what reaches the brain

activity-export.item: one activity record — a search, a visit, a view, a post, a comment, a location event
activity-export.grouping_key: the vendor's activity category plus the day (a day of one category is the unit the importers summarise)
activity-export.canonical: the vendor's record: category, timestamp, title or text, the URL or target, the products and locations the vendor attached
activity-export.text: for a grouped item: the day and category once, then one line per record (`time — title — target`); for a single record: the title and target
edges: target edges to the URLs, places and accounts the records name
activity-export.identity: `<vendor>:<category>:<day>` for a grouped item; `<vendor>:<category>:<record timestamp>:<hash of title+target>` for a single record — a re-import of the same archive is a no-op
activity-export.dividing_line: always a batch over an archive the user downloads (Takeout, an X or Instagram export) → native driver; a tool adds nothing to a file parse

annotation/highlight.item: one highlight or note on a source document
annotation/highlight.grouping_key: the source document (book, article, podcast) — the vendor's book or document id
annotation/highlight.canonical: the vendor's highlight object: id, text, note, location (page, position, timestamp), color or tags, highlighted_at, and the source document's id, title, author and category
annotation/highlight.text: the highlight text; the user's note appended as `Note: …`; the source title and author named once
edges: source-document edge (a document entity per book or article, cached in schemas/readwise-books today)
annotation/highlight.identity: `<vendor>:<highlight id>`; the id is stable across a note edit and a re-export, which is why readwise-capture answers `existed` on a re-delivery
annotation/highlight.dividing_line: the live webhook is a push → tool node (or the native receiver today); the history backfill is a pull the tool can page → tool node, or the native script; both map to one identity so running both makes no duplicate

document/page.grouping_key: the page — sections are the sync unit for the writable direction (SMD-949's section ownership), the page is the capture unit
document/page.canonical: the source form byte-for-byte: the markdown file with its frontmatter (Obsidian, Markdown+git), the block JSON (Notion), the storage format (Confluence), the Atom entry (Blogger) — SMD-1867's round-trip rule: this is the stored truth for a writable page, the text and edges are projections
document/page.text: the body with presentation markup flattened — callouts, embeds, block refs, macros reduced to their visible text — and the title first
edges: link edges from `[[wikilinks]]`, relation properties, issue links, `@page` mentions — the structured layer, imported deterministically and authoritative over an LLM-inferred edge naming the same pair (SMD-1867)
tag edges from `#tags`, labels, frontmatter tags
document/page.identity: `<vendor>:<page id>` where the vendor has one (Notion, Confluence, Blogger); for a file vault, the frontmatter id when present, else the path with a rename detected by content fingerprint (SMD-1813's identity rule: it must survive a rename on either side)
document/page.dividing_line: a vault or export import is a batch → native driver; a live two-way sync (SMD-1814–1818) is a stateful workflow → tool node with the section-ownership and conflict rules of SMD-1813 applied in the brain, not in the node. Splitting a long page by heading is an enrichment past the seam (the atomizer's), not the seam's: the fork's Markdown adapter (`db/ingest-markdown.ts`, SMD-1867) is `1:1`, one file one thought, with chunking left to retrieval (`reembed.ts`); the retired obsidian-vault-import declared `1:many` because its split reached the brain (SMD-2137)
document/page.sink_shape: the page's owned sections written back in the source form; a page the brain did not create is never overwritten whole

web-clip.item: one web page or selection the user chose to keep
web-clip.grouping_key: the URL (canonicalised: scheme and host lowercased, tracking parameters dropped, fragment kept only for a selection anchor)
web-clip.canonical: the URL, the page title, the captured HTML fragment or the readable-article extraction, the selection text when one was made, the capture timestamp
web-clip.text: the title, then the selection if any, else the readable article text
edges: author from the page's metadata when present
web-clip.identity: `web:<canonical url>[#<selection hash>]` — the same page clipped twice is one thought with the later canonical
web-clip.dividing_line: a browser extension push → browser extension; no instance in the tree today (the Chrome extension captures conversations, a different family); the slot names where a clipper lands

calendar/event.item: one calendar event (an instance of a recurring series counts as one)
calendar/event.grouping_key: the recurring series id; a day of events is the unit a briefing summarises
calendar/event.canonical: the event resource: id and iCalUID, calendar id, summary, description, start and end with time zone, recurrence rule and the series id, attendees with response status, location, organizer, created and updated timestamps
calendar/event.text: summary, start–end in the user's zone, location, attendee names, then the description flattened
edges: series edge to the recurring parent
calendar/event.identity: `<vendor>:<calendar id>:<iCalUID>[:<instance start>]` — the iCalUID survives a title change and a move; the instance start distinguishes one occurrence of a series
calendar/event.dividing_line: a look-ahead pull on a cadence → tool node, or the client's calendar MCP when the AI client asks on demand (life-engine today); a change notification push → tool node. Not one of the ticket's seven — added for the calendar read the tree already does
calendar/event.note: Added at classification time: recipes/life-engine reads Google Calendar through the client's MCP connector and none of the seven families named it. The events are read for a briefing, not stored one to one — the family exists so a calendar ingester has a declared slot.

notification-target.item: one outbound notification to a destination that is not a capturable source — SMS, a push service, an arbitrary outbound webhook
notification-target.note: Held in reserve with no instance: every digest in the tree today delivers to a family that is also a source (mail, chat) and is that family's sink capability. An artifact may use this family only once `reserved` is dropped here, which is a spec change, not a connector detail.

slack.note: slack-capture is the source; editorial-policy's optional critical-findings post is the sink. One bot token serves both today, in two artifacts.

discord.note: discord-capture is the source; life-engine's briefings are the sink.

telegram.note: telegram-capture and vercel-neon-telegram's bot route are the source; weekly-digest, life-engine and life-engine-video are the sink. Five artifacts, one vendor driver's worth of client.

gmail.note: email-history-import and gmail-smart-pull are the source (pull); daily-digest's draft is the sink, through the client's Gmail MCP connector.

readwise.note: readwise-capture (push) and readwise-import (pull) are two transports of one source capability; both resolve to `readwise:<highlight id>`.

claude-ai.note: captured by chrome-capture-extension: a manual push of the open exchange and a pull over the internal conversation API for bulk and auto sync.

chatgpt.note: two fetchers, one vendor: chrome-capture-extension (push and pull) and chatgpt-conversation-import (batch) — the same conversation id from either.

gemini.note: chrome-capture-extension: a best-effort manual push and a debugger-observed history pull.

grok.note: grok-export-import over the xAI export, and x-twitter-import's grok-conversations.js — the same vendor from two archives.

x.note: x-twitter-import: tweets are activity, DMs are a message stream.

instagram.note: instagram-import: DMs are a message stream, comments and captions are activity.

blogger.note: journals-blogger-import over the Atom XML export.

google-takeout.note: google-activity-import over a Takeout archive: Search, Gmail activity, Maps, YouTube, Chrome and Gemini Apps as activity records grouped by day.

google-calendar.note: life-engine reads it through the client's Google Calendar MCP connector for the day's briefing.

capabilities.note: Slack Events API → Edge Function; the threaded confirmation is the source's ack

an Edge Function fed by a Discord bot that needs the message-content intent; designated channels only. The folder ships a README and no code, so how the bot hands messages to the function is not in the tree — a push either way
bot webhook; UPDATE_ON_EDIT re-embeds a source-side edit in place through update_thought — the brain never writes to Telegram
highlight webhook; schemas/readwise-books caches the source-document side of the edge
one-shot history backfill over /api/v2/export/; the same identity as the webhook, so the two do not duplicate
manual capture of the open exchange from the DOM
bulk and auto sync over the internal conversation API, one ingest per conversation
manual capture of the open exchange from the DOM
bulk and auto sync over /backend-api/conversations
best-effort manual capture from the Web Components
history sync observed through chrome.debugger — no public API
conversations.json with branches resolved; 0–5 typed thoughts per conversation by LLM extraction
.xlsx export; a Q&A exchange is distilled into standalone thoughts, a memory entry lands as it is
xAI JSON export with MongoDB-style dates; one thought per conversation
tweets.js, batched twenty at a time by date range into one thought
direct-messages.js; a DM conversation of three or more messages is one thought
grok-conversations.js from the X archive; one thought per chat
Gmail API history pull; sender, subject and date as metadata

emits an ingest pack — the closest thing in the tree to the family canonical (RFC 2822 threading headers, structured correspondents); local sensitivity routing before anything leaves the box; atomization of long messages is an enrichment past the seam
My Activity JSON grouped by day and category, each group summarised into one to three thoughts; Gmail and Gemini entries are activity records here, not the mailbox or conversation family
a DM conversation (capped at 200 messages) is one thought
comments in batches of fifty and post captions in batches of thirty
Atom XML export; one thought per post
the day's thoughts → one Gmail draft, created by the AI client's Gmail MCP connector on a scheduled task; brain content leaves the box here — SMD-1903's egress decision applies
importance-ranked synthesis → one sendMessage; optional when no chat id is set
the weekly auditor's critical findings → one chat.postMessage; optional
briefings through Claude Code's Telegram channel plugin; the channel's inbound side is the user talking to the agent, whose own captures go through the brain's MCP surface — not a capture source
the same briefing through the Discord channel plugin
the day's events read through the Google Calendar MCP connector into one briefing; events are not stored one to one
the briefing rendered as a video (Remotion + ElevenLabs — a model provider, not a connector) and sent through the Telegram channel
grammY webhook route into its own Neon brain; /search replies are the brain's read surface over chat, not a sink of brain content to a third party

services.reason: a model or embedding provider — governed by the egress policy (SMD-1903), not the taxonomy
hosting, the runtime or the database the brain runs on

services.pattern: rest api gateway|ob1 agent memory api
services.reason: the brain's own surface (SMD-1931) — a client of it is not a connector
an agent runtime reading and writing memory through the brain's surface

artifacts.recipes/content-fingerprint-dedup: tagged import: the dedup convention the importers cite; no external system
artifacts.recipes/wiki-synthesis: tagged email: synthesises email-thread wikis from thoughts already captured; the mail came in through gmail-smart-pull
artifacts.integrations/rest-api: tagged webhook: the brain's REST surface (SMD-1931); its /ingest is the brain-side capture node, not a vendor
artifacts.recipes/atomizer: tagged gmail: it re-atomizes Gmail thoughts gmail-smart-pull already captured and backfills their correspondents; no Gmail client
artifacts.recipes/infographic-generator: tagged gemini: the Gemini image-generation API is a model provider here, not the Gemini chat product the Chrome extension captures
artifacts.recipes/schema-aware-routing: tagged slack: a metadata-routing pattern in its own project that keeps a slack_ts column for thoughts a Slack capture wrote; the recipe has no Slack client of its own
artifacts.schemas/readwise-books: tagged readwise: the source-document cache table readwise-capture and readwise-import write; a table is not a fetcher
artifacts.primitives/remote-mcp: tagged chatgpt: a guide to connecting AI clients (ChatGPT among them) to the brain's own MCP surface
